# Rights reservation for automated readers. Covers what this fork owns: its own
# documentation, brand assets, and the Gannet Material. It claims nothing about
# upstream Frigate content, which is MIT and none of our business to restrict.
#
# Two conventions are expressed here because crawlers implement different ones:
# the classic robots.txt disallow list, and Content Signals (content-signals.dev),
# which is the vocabulary AI crawlers and the EU AI Act's training-data
# transparency work have converged on.
#
# Content-Signal: general-use=yes, search=yes, ai-train=no, tdmReservation=yes
#
# Read that line as: ordinary use and search indexing are fine, training on this
# content is not, and the TDM reservation stands. general-use=yes is deliberate —
# LICENSE Section 8.3 permits AI inference (reading, explaining, debugging), so a
# blanket none here would claim more than the license does. The rules below are
# the form pre-Content-Signal crawlers understand; they say the same thing.

User-agent: *
Disallow:

User-agent: GPTBot
User-agent: ChatGPT-User
User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
User-agent: GPTBot
User-agent: ClaudeBot
User-agent: Claude-User
User-agent: Claude-Web
User-agent: anthropic-ai
User-agent: Google-Extended
User-agent: PerplexityBot
User-agent: Perplexity-User
User-agent: Applebot-Extended
User-agent: Amazonbot
User-agent: Bytespider
User-agent: CCBot
User-agent: CohereaiBot
User-agent: Diffbot
User-agent: FacebookBot
User-agent: meta-externalagent
User-agent: meta-externalfetcher
User-agent: MistralAI-Bot
User-agent: YouBot
User-agent: Timpibot
User-agent: VelenPublicWebCrawler
User-agent: Webzio-Extended
User-agent: ai-training-bot
User-agent: GPTSearchBot
Disallow: /

# Text-and-data-mining reservation in the W3C TDMRep format: see
# /.well-known/tdmrep.json and the TDM Reservation Protocol spec. Some agents read
# the meta tag instead of the file; both are published, and neither is a license.
